brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: sky/soil split with plants-as-habits creates immediate emotional legibility and a memorable visual system.
Garden Progress card has clean hierarchy, balanced numerics, and a tasteful gradient bar that anchors the busy scene.
Distinct identity — habit trackers rarely commit to a literal scene; the bloom/wilt language has narrative potential.
dominant_weaknesses: Plant rendering is crude: flat star sprites on stick-thin stems read as placeholder graphics, undermining the bloom metaphor entirely.
Floating glassy pill shapes near the title look like broken layout artifacts, not intentional clouds, eroding craft trust.
Horizon line cuts harshly with no atmospheric blending; soil gradient and grass band feel like stacked rectangles rather than a world.
fix_priorities: Redesign plants with real botanical silhouettes, leaves, and growth stages so streaks visibly bloom and neglect wilts.
Fix or remove the stray pill artifacts overlapping the subtitle; ensure clouds read as deliberate shapes.
Soften the sky-to-soil transition with grass tufts, depth, and lighting to make the garden feel inhabited.
Tighten plant spacing and labels — currently row feels mechanical, not organic.
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept is strong, but visceral execution is undercooked and behavioral affordances (how to log a habit) are nearly invisible.
rationale.intent_fit: The metaphor is on-brief but the plants don't yet convincingly express watering, blooming, or wilting states, so the core promise lands only halfway.
